description: Renovate proposes container image, Nextflow and CI tool updates; Dependabot keeps the GitHub Actions and the docs pip file (.github/dependabot.yml).
One PR per tool: no group rules. How a PR is checked and what to revalidate by hand: docs/updating.md.

The images live in versions.env. conf/containers.config and docs/versions.md are generated from it and hold the same strings, so the same dependency is matched in all of them and one PR updates every copy. If a PR touches only versions.env, the generated-file checks fail and name the command to run.
Container images. The four strings match the same image in four files:
docs/versions.md (the Variable, Image and Pinned version cells) and the matrix of container-test.yml.
Each file has a tag form (an optional @sha256 after the tag is kept) and a digest-only form (image@sha256:...).
The image name stops at ':' and '@', so a digest line never becomes a package named '...@sha256'.

customManagers.description: Nextflow: NEXTFLOW_VERSION in versions.env, the setup-nextflow pins in the workflows and the NXF_VER install lines in the docs, all in one PR.
actionlint, downloaded by version in the lint workflow.
gitleaks, downloaded by version in the lint workflow.

description: Biocontainer tags are <version>--<conda build hash>_<build number>. Docker versioning reads the part after '--' as a suffix that must stay the same, and the hash changes between versions, so most of these pins would never see a newer tag.
This versioning ignores the hash and orders by version, then build number. A tag in any other shape (an unsuffixed tag, a four-part version) is not a version here and is never proposed.

packageRules.description: Ensembl VEP tags are release_<major>.<minor>, which docker versioning cannot read. A major (a new Ensembl release) waits for approval on the dependency dashboard: it needs the matching cache (VEP_CACHE_RELEASE in versions.env, about 26 GB) moved in the same PR.

PCGR/CPSR: every update waits for approval on the dependency dashboard, because each release reads its own reference bundle and VEP cache (PCGR_DATA_BUNDLE and PCGR_VEP_CACHE_RELEASE in versions.env). Docker Hub's sigven/pcgr stops at 2.2.5; 2.3.x is published at ghcr.io/sigven/pcgr, which the image matcher reads like any other registry once versions.env names it.

Nextflow: every update waits for approval on the dependency dashboard. A new release can change what the strict config parser accepts, and the validated version is also written in nextflow.config and the Nextflow docs, which need reading by hand.
CI tools take the ci prefix.
